idea: How should we break down .ralph-overview/data.json so the overview-bookkeeper lead does NOT need to load the full task list into context every session, while preserving the bookkeeper's hand-edit ergonomics + the watcher's single-source-of-truth model?

candidateDirections.name: ID-scoped tooling + lazy MCP first; defer source-storage split
candidateDirections.summary: Add tools/data-edit.mjs + MCP write surface (overview.upsert_task, overview.mark_shipped) so writes are task-id addressed; rely on existing read MCP tools so the lead never views the full file. Keep monolithic source. Optionally pair with cheap-D-004 (summary-projection.json + active-tasks.json watcher artifacts).

candidateDirections.name: Per-task source files (.ralph-overview/tasks/<id>.json) with assembled snapshot + INDEX
candidateDirections.summary: Hand-edit one small file per task; watcher assembles snapshot.json + INDEX.md. Atomic per-task edits structurally eliminate cross-task anchor collisions. Highest payoff at scale but most silent-failure surface (dual-authority hazard, watcher rewrite, git-blame noise, 374 KB of prompt bodies bloating per-task files).

candidateDirections.name: Lifecycle-bucketed files (data-active.json + data-merged.json + data-archived.json)
candidateDirections.summary: Simplest split. Hot path drops to 33 tracked tasks. But ship-time atomicity is broken (move task between two files), violating the atomic per-task edit invariant; bucket boundary requires periodic archival sweeps.

candidateDirections.name: Generated projection / 'compute, don't split' (active-tasks.json + summary-projection.json)
candidateDirections.summary: Keep monolithic source; watcher emits a small active subset + a prompts-stripped summary projection so the agent read path is small. Doesn't address write-safety on its own — best as cheap pairing for D-001.

questionsForSynthesis: What exact prompt/request payloads currently include data.json at session start? Run one prompt-trace before sinking effort into D-002/D-003.
Is the operator-perceived slowdown session startup, ready-task selection, one-task expansion, or safe bookkeeping edits? Each has a different fix.
If 1M-context Opus is the lead model, is 173K tokens actually a gating cost at all, or is the real context bloat AGENTS.md + conversation history?
Would a checked-in tools/data-edit.mjs + overview.mark_shipped/upsert_task MCP write surface eliminate the documented wrong-anchor regressions without any storage migration?
Should the bookkeeper's normal read path be tasks/INDEX.md + recommendations.json + overview.parallel_ready_tasks + overview.expand_task_context rather than direct data.json views?
If per-task files (D-002) are chosen later, what prevents a bookkeeper from editing stale data.json out of habit during the 1-minor compatibility window? (Need a hard lint/hook.)
How will migration preserve git blame on task entries extracted from one large array into 147 new files?
Do Claude Code and Copilot CLI resolve @-references identically enough to make lazy @-loading a safe cross-engine design primitive, or should lazy loading live behind MCP only?
